items.title: Security Engineer / Research Engineer, RL Security
items.location_text: San Francisco, CA | New York City, NY | Seattle, WA
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role Reinforcement learning is how Claude learns to reason, write code, and act autonomously over long horizons. At frontier scale, an RL run is a large distributed system: training, sampling, and environment execution run concurrently across a large fleet of accelerators and hosts. As an engineer in RL Engineering, you'll work on keeping that system secure as it scales. This is a hands-on engineering role. You'll work in the RL codebase and the infrastructure underneath it, alongside the engineers and researchers who build and use it. The system is large and changes as fast as the research does, so security work here has to keep up with that pace without costing performance or velocity. We're hiring from two backgrounds: security engineers who want to work on large-scale ML systems, and ML systems or research engineers who want to work on security. Strong candidates have depth in one and real interest in the other. Key responsibilities Design, build, and operate security controls for RL training systems and the infrastructure they run on Work across the stack (orchestration, environments, training, inference) wherever the work is needed Review designs and code across the RL stack, find security problems, and fix them Build shared libraries and tooling that other RL engineers and researchers build on Build the observability needed to understand what these systems are doing Work with researchers and performance engineers to make sure security changes preserve training correctness and performance Write clear design documents for what you build Minimum qualifications Strong software engineering skills in Python and at least one systems language such as Rust, C++, or Go Experience designing, building, and operating large-scale distributed systems or security systems in production Strong understanding of security fundamentals Working knowledge of Linux, containers, and cloud infrastructure Experience debugging complex problems across many hosts and services Ability to reason about tradeoffs between security, performance, and reliability Strong written communication, including design documents Preferred qualifications Experience running ML training or inference infrastructure at scale Experience with infrastructure security, such as isolation, access control, networking, or identity Experience with container orchestration such as Kubernetes, and with sandboxed or virtualized code execution at scale Experience building observability for large fleets Experience supporting research teams or other fast-moving internal users Familiarity with reinforcement learning or large language model training workloads The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $320,000 — $405,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase . As a Complaints Analyst on the Global Complaints team within Customer Experience, you'll investigate and resolve consumer, regulatory, and litigation support complaints to deliver fair outcomes for Coinbase customers. The Global Complaints team is responsible for handling complaints end-to-end across three units, and you'll own assigned cases from intake through resolution, ensuring every customer receives a thorough, accurate, and timely response. This role is fully onsite at Coinbase's London office and requires working in the office five days per week. What you'll do: Investigate and resolve assigned complaints by gathering account data, transaction history, and customer communications, delivering accurate responses within defined SLA timelines Maintain complete case records in Salesforce, including investigation notes, resolution rationale, and customer correspondence, and submit cases for QC review before closure Escalate complex or ambiguous cases to your Supervisor or Complaints Lead with clear documentation of the issue and your initial assessment Flag recurring complaint patterns or potential process gaps to leadership to support continuous improvement across the team Participate in calibration sessions, training, and nesting requirements to stay aligned on evolving quality standards and process updates Required Skills and Experience: 1-2 years of experience in complaints handling, customer service, or dispute resolution within financial services, fintech, or a regulated industry Demonstrated ability to draft clear, accurate written responses to customer complaints, with experience applying documented procedures and escalation paths in a structured environment Track record of meeting SLA and quality targets in a high-volume, QC-reviewed production environment Proficiency in English (reading, writing, and speaking) with the ability to work defined shift patterns as required by the business Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Customer Experience Associate role offers a unique opportunity to build a career in financial services by supporting our users through complex financial topics. As a member of this team, you'll be the company's voice and will use exceptional empathy and product expertise to ensure our users feel understood and valued. Your job is not only to help our customers, but to help us learn as a company from each interaction, so that we can make our customers' experience using our products as seamless as possible. We demonstrate insane customer focus related to a range of needs from simplistic to complex through chat, email, and phone channels. This is an unlicensed role focused on providing high-touch support and guidance on our financial products and platform features. This role is based in our Denver, CO, and Westlake, TX offices, with In-person attendance expected 5 days per week during the 6-week onboarding period. After onboarding in-person attendance is expected at least 3 days a week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Provide an exceptional experience for customers through phone, email, and chat channels, helping them navigate financial topics and platform tools. Drive continuous improvement by identifying and communicating improved ways to serve our users based on real-time feedback and interaction trends. Grow your financial services expertise as you develop deep proficiency in Robinhood’s products and a range of financial concepts. Resolve customer inquiries by exercising independent thought and judgment to find the best solutions in a fast-paced environment. What you bring A passion for supporting customers through various channels and the ability to quickly defuse anxiety through exceptional service skills. Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to explain complex topics clearly. Effectiveness and willingness to adapt to customer experience delivery through both phone and written channels. Comfortable with a fast-paced, evolving landscape and eager to embrace skill development through coaching and feedback. Ability to exercise independent thought, prioritize tasks in a multi-task environment, and adapt to new challenges. A Bachelor’s degree or prior experience in the financial services industry is a plus. Experience working in a customer support environment is preferred. Ability to work the required shift for a 24/7 model What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career. Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching. Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents. Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more. Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits. Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. items.title: Product Data Scientist - Youth, Families and Learning
items.description: About the role We’re looking for a product data scientist to help OpenAI create more value and drive sustainable growth for young people, families, and learners. You’ll drive product data science across under-18 audiences, emerging opportunities for children under 13, family experiences, and learning and education more broadly. You’ll help decide where we should invest, what we should build, and how we’ll know it is working. This means understanding distinct audience needs, identifying promising use cases, and turning evidence into a clear product strategy. Your work will connect discovery and early product development with adoption, retention, and sustained user value. You’ll partner across Chat Product, Growth, Foundations, SafeSys, and other teams, working closely with product managers, engineers, designers, and researchers. The role focuses and owns product value and growth while dedicated teams own policy and safety. In this role, you will: - Shape strategy and prioritize opportunities. Size unmet needs and growth opportunities across audiences, use cases, and product experiences. Help teams choose where to invest and sequence work based on expected user value, reach, evidence, and effort. - Define what value and success mean. Develop an audience-specific measurement framework spanning activation, task success, learning progress, satisfaction, and durable retention. Connect these measures to product goals and assess whether repeat use reflects meaningful benefit. - Understand users and growth drivers. Analyze journeys, funnels, and cohorts to uncover where people find value, where they struggle, and what helps them return. Combine behavioral data with surveys and user research to explain differences across ages, family roles, and learning contexts. - Measure what changes actually cause. Design experiments and holdouts to evaluate product and model changes. Apply causal methods when randomization is impractical, make assumptions explicit, and account for seasonality, audience composition, and effects that differ across segments. - Turn findings into product decisions. Work with partners from initial hypotheses through launch and iteration. Recommend what to build, change, expand, or stop, explaining expected impact, uncertainty, and tradeoffs. Follow through to determine whether decisions delivered the intended results. - Build reliable measurement. Partner with engineering on instrumentation, dataset quality, and consistent audience definitions. Create reusable analyses and dashboards that make progress visible and let teams answer recurring questions independently. - Create alignment across teams. Bring a coherent view of audience value to work spanning multiple roadmaps. Help partners agree on priorities, success criteria, and the next questions to resolve, even when ownership is distributed and evidence is incomplete. You might thrive in this role if you have: - A record of influencing product strategy and improving user outcomes through hands-on data science, including work from an ambiguous question to a decision and measurable impact. - Strong SQL and Python skills, sound statistical judgment, and practical experience with experiments, causal inference, cohort analysis, and measurement design. - The ability to develop useful definitions of product value, validate imperfect proxies, and distinguish short-term metric movement from lasting improvement. - Clear communication and strong product judgment. You can make a recommendation, explain its limits, and influence collaborators across functions without relying on formal authority. - Comfort setting priorities independently across a broad scope, staying close to users, and moving between strategic questions and detailed analytical work. Helpful experience Experience with consumer product growth, youth or family products, learning and education, or generative AI would be valuable. We also welcome experience measuring learning outcomes, combining quantitative and qualitative research, or evaluating products whose value emerges over time. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the role Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades—the largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you're ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading! Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn't a place for complacency, it's where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We're a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. The Trading Tools builds and evolves the core trading platform for active investors. We power best-in-class research, charting, portfolio management, and execution, and we're integrating AI to deliver precise, personalized, and trusted trading experiences at massive scale. As Staff iOS Engineer on the Trading Tools team, you'll serve as the technical lead for mobile. The team owns the surfaces active traders use most: the stock detail page, advanced charts, the trading ladder, portfolio, and watchlists. These are some of the most visited and highest-volume screens in the app. You'll design and build high-performance trading and research interfaces that handle real-time market data, rich charting, and complex portfolio views. You'll work closely with product, design, data science, and backend engineers to ship features that raise the bar on speed, reliability, and usability for pro-grade trading on mobile. You'll also drive architectural decisions that scale with the prod uct and mentor engineers across both platforms, seeing your im pact reach users fast! This role is based in our New York, NY office, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innova tion, and stren gthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you'll do Set the technical vision for mobile across both iOS and Android, and own the quality of execution on both while remaining hands-on in iOS to solve complex technical challenges. Own the architecture of a scalable iOS application supporting core surfaces including stock detail, advanced charts, trading ladder, watchlists, and portfolio. Build a modular, extensible mobile architecture with self-contained components so cross-functional teams can build, test, and ship independently. Drive cross-platform consistency by aligning iOS and Android on architecture, data contracts, feature parity, and release sequencing. Improve application performance, real-time data handling, observability, and release stability across core trading workflows (including rendering, launch time, and page-load time). Evolve charting and research experiences tailored for active traders. Lead the integration of AI-driven capabilities into core trading, research, and portfolio workflows on mobile. Lead technical planning and guide system design reviews, implementation discussions, and incident resolution for high-stakes trading features. Partner with product managers, designers, backend engineers, and data teams to run experiments and drive product release decisions. Mentor iOS and Android engineers through code reviews, technical feedback, and structured development support, helping senior engineers expand toward staff-level scope while defining engineering standards and documentation. Influence mobile platform direction beyond the team by collaborating with adjacent organizations and company-wide initiatives. What you bring 8+ years of professional experience developing iOS applications, including extensive experience building and maintaining large-scale apps with Swift and modern iOS frameworks (UIKit, SwiftUI). Proven experience owning the technical direction of a product area or platform. Experience designing mobile systems with clear architecture patterns, scalable component design, and maintainable testing strategies for data-intensive or real-time use cases. Track record of leading technical initiatives across multiple teams or platforms, balancing short-term delivery with long-term platform improvements. Strong working knowledge of Android development principles to set technical direction and collaborate effectively with Android engineers. Demonstrated capability to collaborate with product, design, backend, and infrastructure partners to deliver customer-focused technical solutions. Excellent communication skills with the ability to translate complex trading concepts into intuitive mobile experiences. History of mentoring engineers and fostering engineering excellence. Nice to have: experience with financial platforms, trading systems, or real-time market data products. Nice to have: experience with server-driven UI, embedded web or React Native surfaces, live audio/video streaming, or building LLM-powered product features. items.title: Compliance Program Manager — Regulatory Compliance
items.description: About the team Governance, Risk, and Compliance (GRC) builds compliance programs and provides assurance for OpenAI’s technology, people, and products. We combine technical understanding with practical operations to reduce risk, support product and research teams, and produce reliable evidence of how our controls work. About the role As a Regulatory Compliance Program Manager, you will build and operate programs that turn regulatory requirements into clear responsibilities, effective processes, and evidence that can withstand external scrutiny. Your work will focus on AI safety/security and content moderation, with privacy operations as an adjacent area. You will partner with Legal and the teams that build and operate our products to scope the work, maintain accurate control narratives, prepare regulatory responses, and lead external assessments for your assigned portfolio. You should be comfortable owning delivery, explaining tradeoffs, and changing your recommendation when the evidence changes. Success means controls have accountable owners, evidence stays current, and teams can respond accurately without repeatedly rebuilding the same work. The initial portfolio and expectations will be agreed with the hiring manager. In this role, you will: - Lead an agreed portfolio of AI safety/security and content-compliance work, including programs associated with the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, with Legal and relevant experts confirming applicable requirements. - Translate requirements into scoped programs, operating processes, control and evidence responsibilities, milestones, and clear escalation paths. - Build and maintain accurate control narratives and traceable evidence for regulatory requests, reporting, audits, and assessments. - Lead preparation and delivery for external compliance assessments, coordinate the responsible teams, and track gaps through verified resolution or an explicitly owned decision. - Prioritize the work that materially improves compliance outcomes and reduces risk; explain what should proceed, change, or wait and why. - Develop evidence-backed recommendations with Legal, Product, Security, Safety, Integrity, Privacy, and other functional teams. Obtain decisions from the authorized owners for legal interpretation, external representations, and risk acceptance. - Improve operational workflows for content and privacy compliance while keeping implementation and operation of controls with the appropriate functional owners. - Simplify and automate repeated administrative work, test the results, and verify that the improvement is adopted and produces accurate, reliable outputs. - Learn the GRC security-control environment and participate in the team’s on-call rotation, with scope and expectations explained during the hiring process. - Communicate clearly, surface uncertainty early, incorporate feedback, and develop the domain knowledge needed for the next priority. You might thrive in this role if you: - Have practical experience building and operating AI safety/security and content-moderation programs, and can explain your own decisions, contribution, and results. - Have used agentic tooling to automate and improve to scaled processes - Understand relevant technical concepts across model evaluation, training and release, safety controls, content moderation, and post-launch operations, and can explain where specialist input is needed. - Have a strong understanding of relevant AI safety, content, and privacy requirements, including the EU AI Act, DSA, OSA, and SB 53, and experience translating them into operating processes and controls with domain experts and Legal. - Have led regulatory responses and external compliance audits, and can distinguish supported claims from evidence gaps. - Have delivered complex cross-functional programs, scoped practical first increments, and adapted priorities when constraints changed. - Have improved or automated an operational workflow and verified its accuracy, usefulness, and ongoing ownership. - Can maintain precise records, navigate technical/compliance documentation and contract language, follow through on commitments, and judge what to resolve directly or escalate. - Communicate clearly in writing and conversation with technical teams, Legal, leadership, and external stakeholders; explain evidence, uncertainty, recommendations, and tradeoffs. - Work constructively through disagreement, learn from feedback, and take responsibility for outcomes. Privacy program-management experience is a plus. About OpenAI OpenAI is an AI research and deployment company dedicated to ensuring that general-purpose artificial intelligence benefits all of humanity. We push the boundaries of the capabilities of AI systems and seek to safely deploy them to the world through our products. AI is an extremely powerful tool that must be created with safety and human needs at its core, and to achieve our mission, we must encompass and value the many different perspectives, voices, and experiences that form the full spectrum of humanity. We are an equal opportunity employer, and we do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, color, national origin, sex, sexual orientation, age, veteran status, disability, genetic information, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. For additional information, please see OpenAI’s Affirmative Action and Equal Employment Opportunity Policy Statement https://cdn.openai.com/policies/eeo-policy-statement.pdf. Background checks for applicants will be administered in accordance with applicable law, and qualified applicants with arrest or conviction records will be considered for employment consistent with those laws, including the San Francisco Fair Chance Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act, for US-based candidates. In addition, job duties require access to secure and protected information technology systems and related data security obligations. About the role Anthropic’s mission is to ensure that the world safely makes the transition through transformative AI. Security is one of the clearest places where that mission plays out: the same capabilities that help attackers move faster can help defenders move faster too, and helping them use those capabilities safely and well is what this team is for. Security teams are among the earliest and most demanding users of frontier AI. They use Claude to review code at scale, find vulnerabilities before attackers do, and work through alert queues their analysts can’t keep up with. Anthropic’s Applied AI organization is building a dedicated Security team to help them do this well, and we are looking for its first leader. You will build this team from zero. You’ll decide which security customers the team serves first, who you hire and in what order, and how the team works with Sales, Applied AI Engineering, and our security, legal, and trust partners. You’ll also stay hands-on with a few of our most important security customers, because what you learn in those accounts becomes the playbook for everyone else. items.title: Senior Accountant - Fiat & EMI Entities
items.description: Remote | EU/EEA or UK | Crypto & Payments | EMI Accounting | Full-time Our client is an established, profitable fintech operating at the intersection of crypto and traditional payments. It runs a consumer on/off-ramp platform and a fast-growing B2B infrastructure business: APIs and white-label solutions that let exchanges, neobanks, PSPs, wallets and other platforms embed regulated crypto and fiat services. The company is authorised under MiCA and PSD2 in the EU and is now expanding its fiat business through new e-money licences in the EU and the UK. The culture is high-ownership and low-bureaucracy, with fast decisions and no micromanagement. About the role This is a senior, hands-on accounting role with a clear mandate: own the books of the company’s fiat entities, from licence to steady state. You will take end-to-end ownership of four entities: two e-money institutions in the EU and the UK that are in the licensing pipeline, plus fiat entities in the US and Canada. For the new EMIs, the first months are about building accounting properly from an empty ledger. Safeguarding and prudential requirements apply from the first day of trading, and volumes ramp quickly once licences land. If you want to set up EMI accounting from scratch rather than run a finished process, this role is built for you. You will report to the Accounting and Financial Reporting Lead and work as an individual contributor within a small accounting team. Each accountant owns specific legal entities end to end, and responsibilities do not overlap. What you will own - Entity accounting: day-to-day accounting for four fiat entities in Xero (multi-currency), from set-up through steady state. - New entity set-up: chart of accounts, bank mapping, close calendar and statutory and tax filing calendar for each newly licensed entity. - EMI accounting and reporting: safeguarding and client-money reconciliations designed with Treasury, inputs for own-funds and capital-adequacy calculations, and EMI regulatory returns to the national regulator and the FCA, end to end. - Month-end close: for every entity, covering bank reports mapped by counterparty and intercompany, accruals, prepayments, loans, payroll entries and FX revaluation. - Intercompany: recording and reconciling heavy intercompany flows with Treasury, and supporting transfer pricing documentation. - Local statutory and tax compliance: EU and UK annual accounts, VAT and statistical reporting, Companies House and HMRC deadlines, and year-end inputs for the US and Canada. You will prepare the data and own the filing calendar, working with external tax advisers. - Invoice control: checking that supplier invoices meet local tax requirements before payment. - Audit and group reporting: consolidation inputs, audit schedules and auditor queries for your entities. - Management accounts: monthly entity-level accounts, analytical review of P&L and balance-sheet movements, and investigation of unusual items before close sign-off. - Process build: documented close procedures and controls for each new entity, designed to scale after licensing. What we are looking for - Hands-on accounting experience for a live EMI in the EU or UK. This includes EMI regulatory returns you owned end to end and safeguarding or client-money reconciliations you ran yourself, not through an outsourced provider. - Experience producing own-funds or capital-requirement inputs for an EMI. - 5+ years of in-house accounting with independent general ledger ownership and month-end close. - Strong IFRS (UK GAAP / FRS 102 accepted) and a working understanding of US GAAP simplifications. You can analyse new transactions, decide the accounting treatment and document your position. - Multi-entity, multi-currency accounting, including intercompany reconciliation, FX revaluation and group consolidation (eliminations, foreign-currency translation). - Strong balance-sheet ownership: account reconciliations, ageing analysis, investigation of unreconciled items and balance substantiation. - Experience reconciling high-volume payment data to bank accounts and the general ledger. - A fintech or payments background. - A builder mindset: comfortable setting up processes from scratch rather than expecting them to be in place. - Fluent English. - Existing right to work and residence in the EU/EEA or the UK. Nice to have - Latvian statutory and tax knowledge (VAT, statistical reports, benefits in kind) or Latvian language. - Experience setting up accounting for a newly licensed EMI or PI. - Experience running a multi-country filing calendar with external tax advisers. - Xero, plus ERP or reconciliation tooling. - Exposure to crypto or to international groups with heavy intercompany flows. - Big 4 or audit background. What’s on offer - End-to-end ownership of four entities, including building EMI accounting from day one. - A fully remote setup, with a flat structure, fast decisions and trust-based ways of working. - 20 paid working days of annual leave, paid sick leave and health insurance. - Professional development opportunities, team events and an English course. - A fast, transparent hiring process.

Money moves every day across dozens of bank accounts, payment providers, acquirers, exchange venues and wallets, in several currencies and jurisdictions. Your job is to make sure it is in the right place, in the right amount, at the right time, and that the company can prove it to an auditor or a regulator. You will take full ownership of operational payments, build regular cash and crypto reporting for Finance leadership, and get safeguarding reconciliation ready for the company’s upcoming e-money licences. This is an individual contributor role with real ownership: you will not just run existing processes, you will help redesign them. What you will own - Operational payments: the end-to-end invoice and salary payment cycle, including validation, approval routing, FX and release across banks and EMIs, as well as beneficiary verification, dual authorisation, returns and stuck payments. - Payment process redesign: working with Finance leadership to build a faster, well-controlled payment process: higher payment frequency, invoice checks with accounting before payment, backup approvers and the four-eyes principle kept at all times. - Cash and crypto reporting: collecting balances across banks, acquirers, PSPs, exchanges and custody accounts, and producing a signed-off cash flow report with analytics on changes in cash and crypto positions. - Safeguarding and segregation: daily safeguarding reconciliation for e-money entities once operational, and client-asset segregation and reconciliation under MiCA and PSD2, with records that stand up to review. - Regulatory and audit support: recurring returns for licensed entities and the treasury evidence pack for audit and regulator requests. - Liquidity: short-term forecasting, pre-funding of settlement and trading accounts, sweeps, and stablecoin and hot/cold float management in line with policy. - Controls and improvement: treasury policies, authority matrices and SOPs, and moving reporting and reconciliation off spreadsheets together with Finance Systems and Engineering. What we are looking for - 3–5 years in treasury or payment operations, ideally at a crypto or fintech company. - Hands-on payment execution in a company role: approval workflows, banking portals, payment file formats and segregation of duties. - Real crypto operations experience: exchange and custody accounts, stablecoin settlement, hot/cold wallet operations, on-chain verification, and network specifics such as fees, finality, memo/tag and stuck transactions. - Ownership of regular balance reporting and reconciliation in a multi-currency, multi-account environment, including resolving breaks. - Experience in a regulated environment: regulatory reporting, safeguarding or client-money rules, and audit or regulator requests. - Strong Excel or Google Sheets skills. - Exceptional attention to detail, precision under cut-off pressure and full discretion with sensitive financial information. - Fluent English. - Based in a time zone close to CET/EET. Nice to have - Hands-on PSD2 or EMI safeguarding reconciliation, including UK safeguarding. - MiCA/CASP crypto-asset segregation and reporting. - Experience redesigning a payment or approval process together with accounting. - Building cash flow reports and dashboards; SQL beyond the basics. - Fireblocks or a similar custody/MPC platform. - A treasury certification such as ACT or CTP. What’s on offer - Full ownership of treasury operations in a regulated crypto and payments business. - A role where you shape processes and controls, not just follow them. - A remote setup, or hybrid at the company’s European HQ, with a flat structure and fast decisions. - A full-time contract with a performance bonus. - Paid leave, health insurance and a certification budget. - A clear hiring process: HR interview, a joint interview with Treasury and Finance leadership, and a reference check. Because the role involves access to company accounts, a pre-employment background check follows the offer.

The BSA/AML and OFAC programme is already in place: policies, risk assessment, SAR process, sanctions screening, training records and an independent review. Your mission is to keep it examination-ready on any given day and to raise it to the standard that supports US growth with banking partners, card acquirers and new integrations. You will make filing, exit and escalation decisions independently. What’s on offer - A statutory role with real authority, direct Board access and documented independence. - Real ownership: you run the US programme and shape how it supports the company’s growth. - A remote setup within the US, with periodic in-person time at the European HQ.

Practical expertise in balancing different slot formats and mechanics, including Megaways, cluster pays, grid slots, bonus buys, jackpots, free spins, multipliers, and cascading features - Strong understanding of reel and paytable configuration, bonus buy and ante bet mathematics, and multiple RTP variants, with the ability to balance feature frequency, payout sizes, and overall player experience - Advanced experience in mathematical validation and high-volume simulations, including analytical RTP verification, Monte Carlo methods involving billions of spins, variance analysis, confidence intervals, and convergence assessment - Familiarity with gaming certification standards and testing procedures, including requirements associated with GLI, BMM, eCOGRA, iTech Labs, and preparation of mathematical reports and PAR sheets - Ability to independently manage mathematical development throughout the complete game lifecycle, from initial design to final certification - About the role Platform Safety builds the infrastructure that lets Anthropic bring its most capable models to more people, safely and securely. Our systems decide both who can access our most advanced models, and what capabilities they can access, wherever Claude is available. That includes identity and business verification, trusted access programs, and the core services that grant, hold and enforce model access across our products. These systems already power the Cyber Verification Program, which now includes Project Glasswing, and the Life Sciences Verification Program with further more advanced use cases in development. As a Staff+ engineer, you'll help set the technical direction for this work. The foundations are live and adoption is growing quickly, so the next challenge is scale: making access a matter of configuration instead of code, making verification reusable, and giving customers a consistent experience on every surface. You'll work closely with safeguards, product, design and research to turn safety policy into systems that are easy to use and enforce. You'll also take new 0 → 1 efforts from idea to delivery as new capabilities and programs emerge. What you'll do You'll design, build and operate the systems that decide who gets access to our most capable models. You'll build the platform that lets teams across Anthropic launch and run trusted access programs, moving access rules out of code and into data so that launching a new model or complex program is simple and scalable. You'll build out our identity and business verification system (KYC/KYB) as a reusable service that any program can use, which means integrating verification vendors, protecting sensitive personal data, expanding into new regions, and building fair review and appeal paths for customers. You'll also evolve the core services behind every access decision, including the services that grant and hold access and the customer and user identity models they rely on, and keep them highly available and consistent across our own products and cloud platforms. You'll shape the architecture through clear written proposals, review key designs, and mentor engineers on a growing team. You'll also share on-call, lead incident response, and support emerging new programs. You might be a good fit if you: Have a minimum of 8 years of practical experience as a backend or platform engineer, ideally at tech lead level or equivalent, and are comfortable working across the stack when the problem calls for it Have strong product sense, and work closely with cross-functional partners, including non-engineers, to shape and execute strategy in new domains Use AI tools as a regular part of how you design, build and review software Have designed and operated production distributed systems on a critical path, where correctness, latency and availability all matter Take full ownership of your work, from design through build, deployment, operations and iteration Navigate ambiguity and make sound technical decisions independently, have set technical direction that other engineers and teams adopted, and have ideally operated in both 0 → 1 and more mature settings Care about building robust, scalable systems that other engineers and businesses love to use Care about the societal impacts of your work and Anthropic's mission to build safe, beneficial AI Strong candidates may also have: Identity, access control or authorization systems at scale Fraud, risk, trust and safety, or KYC/KYB systems, including working with verification vendors Regulated or compliance-sensitive environments, including handling sensitive personal data Integrating with cloud platforms or partner ecosystems such as AWS, Google Cloud and Azure Deadline to apply: None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. Location Preference: Preference will be given to candidates based in NY, SEA, SF or the Bay Area given the current location of team. The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: $405,000 — $485,000 USD Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. items.description: Ready to do the most impactful work of your career? At Coinbase , we are uncompromising on our mission to increase economic freedom. The bar is high, the environment is intense, and we like it that way. This isn't a place for complacency, it’s a place to be pushed past your perceived limits. If you're ready to build the future of finance alongside people who refuse to settle for "good enough," you belong here. Coinbase is a remote-first, but not remote-only company. Expect to get together quarterly for intense in-person working sessions called “surges.” learn more about working at Coinbase . We are hiring Staff Software Engineers across several teams within the Developer Infrastructure group in Platform. You'll own the tools and systems every Coinbase engineer depends on to build and ship software. This team is responsible for scalable CI and build infrastructure and deployment orchestration, where a single improvement compounds across thousands of engineers. You'll set technical direction for the group's most complex, cross-cutting problems and lead their delivery from ambiguous problem statements through production operation. What you'll do: Own core developer infrastructure platforms, including CI/build systems and deployment orchestration, across the full lifecycle from design through production operation. Identify the group's highest-leverage problems, turn ambiguous and unscoped challenges into concrete technical roadmaps, and drive alignment across dependent teams. Drive step-change improvements to the metrics every engineer feels: build and CI wall time, deploy speed and safety, and developer feedback latency. Lead strategic, cross-cutting initiatives end to end, including large-scale platform migrations, landing them across many teams alongside the engineers doing the work. Raise the reliability bar for developer infrastructure by owning SLOs, observability, and on-call, designing systems that recover fast rather than cascade into company-wide incidents. Partner with engineering customers, EMs, and leadership across Coinbase to shape technical strategy and drive org-wide adoption of what you build, while mentoring engineers through design review, pairing, and shared ownership. Required Skills and Experience: 8+ years building and operating production distributed systems, with hands-on proficiency in Go or a comparable systems language and direct experience in CI/CD, build systems, or deployment tooling. Track record of designing and shipping high-impact backend or platform systems that many engineers and services depend on, owning them from ambiguous problem statements through long-term production operation. Demonstrated technical leadership on cross-team initiatives: setting architectural direction, driving org-wide alignment, and making decisions that held up at scale, while staying close enough to the code to lead by example. Deep operational expertise with production systems where downtime has a broad blast radius, including designing for reliability, observability, and fast recovery from day one. Proven ability to drive alignment on ambiguous, cross-functional problems and to raise the technical bar around you through mentorship, design review, and clear written and verbal communication. Utilizes generative AI responsibly, maintaining human oversight to deliver business-ready outputs and drive measurable improvements in workflow efficiency, cost, and quality. items.description: OVERVIEW The Workplace Experience team powers and connects the workday for all Perplexity employees across our global offices. We are hospitality and experience-driven at the core. We are made up of People people, meaning that we love supporting each other and all of the People in our workplace. We take on the good and the bad with optimism and with a positive, kind approach to solving problems, dealing with the obstacles handed to us, and proactively creating good around us. We think about each moment through the lens of our colleagues (our customers) so that we can create thoughtful and memorable experiences no matter what task we have at hand. Our San Francisco office of approximately 200+ seats is located in SOMA. The SF Sr. Workplace Coordinator will be a part of the global Workplace team, and will be responsible for all office operational, coordination, and administrative tasks while cultivating a beautiful, positive, and productive workplace. WHAT YOU’LL DO - Keep the SF office running in partnership with the Workplace Coordinator, covering day-to-day reception, operations, vendor relationships and services, employee health and safety compliance, and facility maintenance - Create a wonderful workplace experience for employees, visitors, recruits, customers and vendors, keeping the office tidy, clean, organized and polished throughout the day - Open and close the office daily (8:30am - 5:00pm), and be on site when no one else is for special projects, maintenance or moves - Administer SF office access and visitor management, including badge setup and removal, guest registration and building-security lists, in partnership with Physical Security and IT - Manage team mail and deliveries, from small packages to large and freight deliveries, by triaging, distributing and keeping it all organized - Manage inventory and order all office and kitchen supplies while tracking spend and working within the office budget, and help remotely with supply ordering for small neighboring offices - Build relationships with building management, maintenance and cleaning staff, and external parties such as contractors and suppliers, including quality control, vendor accountability and delivering feedback - Manage vendor and contractor paperwork and logistics, including insurance certificates, contractor access and freight elevator bookings - Help coordinate design and construction projects and act as the on-site contact - Own the SF and Palo Alto workplace ticket queue, triaging, resolving and routing requests in a kind and timely manner and keeping requesters updated through close - Own SF office communications and documentation, including the office guide or wiki, Slack announcements to employees and leaders, and building notices - Organize, monitor and communicate facility and building safety preparedness to employees - Produce thoughtful and inclusive office experiences and events, working with the Workplace team to stay consistent with other offices and the global strategy - Visit the Palo Alto office as needed to support on-site operations, supplies and employee requests - Help with ad-hoc projects when time allows, and contribute in ways beyond this high-level overview of the role WHAT YOU BRING - 5-7 years of experience working in facilities, workplace operations, office administration, or hospitality fields - Proficiency with G-Suite Products or the ability to learn software quickly - Excellent organization, planning and prioritization skills - Exceptionally strong ownership and can-do attitude with an operational mindset - Comfortable working autonomously, juggling multiple tasks under tight deadlines, switching gears at the drop of a hat, and having a “no task too small” mentality - Willingness to jump in where needed, picking up projects and checking things off lists even when it lands on your plate unexpectedly - Excellent written, non-verbal, and verbal communication skills; the ability to work well with various personality types, and are receptive to feedback...all while maintaining a high degree of professionalism and confidentiality - Genuine passion for supporting others and a contagiously positive attitude - The capability to anticipate others' needs and act with patience, kindness, and firmness - An eye for detail with regards to all things from process to projects to space to events - The ability to maintain a professional and kind game face even when things aren’t going as planned or desired; a propensity for problem solving quickly and quietly - A solid sense of self awareness and the desire for feedback to adapt and grow

items.title: Technical Program Manager
items.location_text: Menlo Park, CA; New York, NY
items.description: Join us in building the future of finance. Our mission is to democratize finance for all. An estimated $124 trillion of assets will be inherited by younger generations in the next two decades. The largest transfer of wealth in human history. If you’re ready to be at the epicenter of this historic cultural and financial shift, keep reading. About the team + role We are building an elite team, applying frontier technologies to the world’s biggest financial problems. We’re looking for bold thinkers. Sharp problem-solvers. Builders who are wired to make an impact. Robinhood isn’t a place for complacency, it’s where ambitious people do the best work of their careers. We’re a high-performing, fast-moving team with ethics at the center of everything we do. Expectations are high, and so are the rewards. Brokerage sits at the heart of Robinhood, powering how millions of customers invest and interact with financial products. The Brokerage Technical Program Management team is small and collaborative, and it works side by side with senior engineers, engineering managers, product leaders, and Brokerage leadership on complex technical and execution challenges. We partner closely with design, customer experience, and operations teams to bring ambitious work to life. The team is still shaping how it plans, executes, launches, and uses AI, so there’s real room to build the playbook rather than inherit one! As a Technical Program Manager on Brokerage, you’ll own and drive cross-functional engineering programs from kickoff through launch. You’ll keep plans, milestones, risks, and dependencies clear and visible, and you’ll turn complex technical work into crisp updates for leadership and partner teams. The mix of programs will flex with company priorities, and you’ll be trusted with real ownership early on. You’ll also have the chance to rethink traditional TPM workflows with AI, from planning to launch readiness. Expect close mentorship and a clear runway to grow your career here! This role is based in our New York, NY OR Menlo Park, CA offices, with in-person attendance expected at least 3 days per week. At Robinhood, we believe in the power of in-person work to accelerate progress, spark innovation, and strengthen community. Our office experience is intentional, energizing, and designed to fully support high-performing teams. What you’ll do Drive execution across multiple cross-functional engineering teams, from kickoff through launch Own program plans, milestones, risks, and dependencies, and keep them visible to stakeholders Coordinate with product, design, customer experience, operations, and engineering partners Write clear narratives, status updates, and communications for leadership and partner teams Spot gaps and unblock work so programs keep moving with minimal oversight Help shape how the Brokerage TPM team plans, executes, and launches, including how it uses AI to improve planning, dependency management, risk detection, launch readiness, and reporting What you bring 5+ years of experience in technical program management or a similar role, driving complex cross-functional engineering programs Strong grasp of system design, with the ability to follow and contribute to engineering conversations (no coding required) Working familiarity with AWS and core infrastructure concepts Exceptional written and verbal communication, including concise narratives and executive-ready updates that translate complex technical work Strong ownership of outcomes, with the initiative to identify next steps, close gaps, and resolve blockers without waiting to be asked A proven record of running programs with minimal oversight and following through on commitments until problems are resolved Comfort stepping outside a narrowly defined scope when the program needs it Strong organizational skills, with the ability to create structure and clarity across complex, multi-team programs without adding unnecessary process Curiosity and excitement about using AI as part of how you work What we offer Challenging, high-impact work to grow your career Performance driven compensation with multipliers for outsized impact, bonus programs, equity ownership, and 401(k) matching Top Tier benefits to fuel your work, including 100% paid health insurance for employees with 90% coverage for dependents Access to the Robinhood Employee Fund that gives eligible US employees the opportunity to invest in a private employee fund that provides exposure to Robinhood Ventures funds. Access to the best AI tools on the market and continuous AI skill-building for every employee, technical or not. Lifestyle wallet - a highly flexible benefits spending account for wellness, learning, and more Employer-paid life & disability insurance, fertility benefits, and mental health benefits Time off to recharge including company holidays, paid time off, sick time, parental leave, and more! Exceptional office experience with catered meals, events, and comfortable workspaces. In addition to the base pay range listed below, this role is also eligible for bonus opportunities + equity + benefits. Base pay for the successful applicant will depend on a variety of job-related factors, which may include education, training, experience, location, business needs, or market demands. The expected base pay range for this role is based on the location where the work will be performed and is aligned to one of 3 compensation zones. For other locations not listed, compensation can be discussed with your recruiter during the interview process. If our mission energizes you and you’re ready to build the future of finance, we look forward to seeing your application. AI Usage Disclosure: Robinhood uses artificial intelligence (AI) tools to support parts of our recruiting process. These tools enhance the efficiency and consistency of our hiring process; however, all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. Robinhood provides equal opportunity for all applicants, offers reasonable accommodations upon request, and complies with applicable equal employment and privacy laws. Inclusion is built into how we hire and work—welcoming different backgrounds, perspectives, and experiences so everyone can do their best. Please review the Privacy Policy for your country of application.

items.description: ABOUT MISTRAL Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. We partner with enterprises tackling the hardest problems across high-stakes industries like finance, manufacturing, defense, healthcare, and the public sector, co-creating customized AI systems that they can run on their terms. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited. THE ROLE Mistral AI is seeking Applied Scientists and Research Engineers focused on formal methods. You will design, train, and deploy SOTA large language models and apply them to diverse use cases. You'll work cross-functionally with internal and external science, engineering, and product teams to deliver high-impact AI solutions. items.title: International Compensation Partner
items.description: About Anthropic Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems. About the role We are seeking an experienced Compensation Partner to join our Total Rewards team and lead compensation for our international locations as Anthropic builds out its global presence. This role will support our international org on the strategy, design and execution of Anthropic's compensation programs, adapting a global framework to markets that work differently. It is a great fit for someone who has seen compensation excellence at scale and has operated in rapidly scaling, high-ambiguity environments with evolving scope. You'll serve as connective tissue between a fast-moving regional business and a global Total Rewards team. Responsibilities Own compensation for our international locations (such as Germany, France, UK, Ireland, Japan, Australia, India, and beyond as the international team grows), building scalable processes and infrastructure across key markets Support Anthropic's overall compensation framework, including salary, variable compensation and equity-based programs, and adapt it for local market practice, legal requirements, and competitive dynamics while keeping a consistent global philosophy Operate as a strategic compensation business partner to international leadership, People Partners, and recruiting, building relationships and context to navigate ambiguous problems and recommend solutions tailored to Anthropic's unique needs Own comp cycle execution end-to-end for international employees, including local market benchmarking, budget modeling, currency considerations, manager enablement, edge-case resolution, and exec-ready rollups, in partnership with the broader Total Rewards team Navigate complex international regulatory environments, ensuring compliance with local pay and employment requirements across markets, including works councils, statutory pay and benefits requirements, pay transparency obligations, and country-specific equity and tax considerations, in close partnership with Legal and Equity Build and maintain international benchmarking methodology Provide subject matter expertise and counsel to People Partners, managers and leadership on pay decisions, policy and guideline interpretations, and job evaluations across regions Create compelling data narratives and presentations for leadership, translating complex analysis into clear strategic recommendations Partner cross-functionally to develop scalable processes that enable consistent, high-quality compensation decision-making across the organization Develop and deliver enablement on our compensation philosophy and programs across Anthropic for your business stakeholders You may be a good fit if you: Have deep expertise in compensation, preferably in a high-growth environment, with direct experience across multiple countries or regions Have a strong working knowledge of international compensation practices and the regulatory landscape across key markets, including works councils and pay transparency requirements Have experience localizing global compensation programs Excel at collaborating across time zones with exceptional cross-cultural communication skills Have strong collaboration and program management skills, with a track record of taking on ambiguously-scoped projects and taking ownership to deliver great results Thrive in strategic thinking while remaining comfortable with hands-on execution and detailed analysis Are an exceptional communicator, particularly in writing Are comfortable with ambiguity and thrive in fast-paced, high-growth environments Strong candidates may also: Speak languages relevant to our international markets (fluency in German, French, Japanese, or other languages is a plus) Have supported a US-headquartered company through rapid international expansion The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role. Annual Salary: £190,000 — £190,000 GBP Logistics Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices. Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this. We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team. Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings. How we're different We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills. The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences. Come work with us! Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.
